The manipulation of time in the story is skilfully balanced to serve its emotional and thematic core. The author uses **compression of time** early on (summarizing a three-hour hike and twelve years of solitude in the opening paragraph) and within Arthur's dialogue and internal reflections (condensing decades of his career, his brother's death, and his failed marriage into a few paragraphs). Conversely, the author slows the pacing down when Arthur discovers the crash, examining small sensory details (the ticking wheel, the spilled contents of the tote bag) to create an atmosphere of profound stillness. Finally, the forty-five-minute wait for the state patrol is smoothly compressed through a mix of real-time monologue and summary ("as the minutes elongated"), allowing the reader to feel the weight of the wait without the narrative dragging.
